# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date this letter is sent]

**To:** Regence BlueShield — Member Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Fax: 1-888-496-1542 (per the Oregon appeal form; I will use the form and return address for Washington from regence.com/member/members/member-appeals)

**From:** Jordan Brooks
Member ID: W436997835
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

---

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 23, 2026**
**Reference number:** POC-41FE448BEA-64337
**Service denied:** Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
**Governing policy:** *Femoroacetabular Impingement Surgery, Surgery Policy No. 160 (SUR160)* — https://blue.regence.com/trgmedpol/surgery/sur160.pdf

---

Dear Reviewer,

I am appealing Regence BlueShield's denial of prior authorization for the hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated August 23, 2026 states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the medical records already submitted match the plan's own published criteria point for point.

Below I have quoted the plan's criteria from *Femoroacetabular Impingement Surgery, Surgery Policy No. 160 (SUR160)* exactly as the policy states them, and then set out the documentation in my chart that corresponds to each one.

## The plan's criteria and the evidence in my records

**1. Pain worsened by flexion activities that limits my activities**

The policy states:

> "A. Moderate-to-severe hip pain that is worsened by flexion activities (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) that significantly limits activities"

My records document nine months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest. They describe sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and with pivoting, and that I cannot run or squat. Sitting and squatting are the two examples the policy itself gives.

**2. Unresponsive to conservative therapy**

The policy states:

> "B. Unresponsive to conservative therapy for at least 3 months or clinical documentation that conservative therapy is contraindicated (e.g., history of falls due to mechanical instability of hip joint)"

My records document supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, 14 weeks in length, from April 9, 2026 through July 16, 2026, with 20 visits completed. This is recorded in the physical therapy discharge note. In addition, I took NSAIDs for eight months with inadequate relief, and I had a corticosteroid injection on April 21, 2026 that gave only two weeks of partial relief. The 14 weeks of supervised therapy exceeds the three-month period the policy sets, and my symptoms have continued to progress despite it.

**3. Positive impingement sign on examination**

The policy states:

> "C. Positive impingement sign on clinical examination (i.e., pain elicited with 90 degrees of flexion and internal rotation and adduction of the femur)"

My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. If the reviewer needs the examining physician's specific wording for the maneuver performed, it appears in the office note of [date of the office visit documenting the examination] by Dr. Marchetti, and I ask that this note be re-reviewed rather than the request being closed for want of it.

**4. Imaging documenting cam-type or pincer-type FAI morphology**

The policy states:

> "1. Imaging (conventional x-rays, MRI, MRI arthrogram) documents morphology indicative of cam-type or pincer-type FAI (See List of Information Needed for Review); and"

and, in the list of information needed for review:

> "• Imaging (conventional x-rays, MRI, MRI arthrogram) that documents morphology indicative of cam-type or pincer-type FAI such as one or more of the following:"

One of the findings the policy names in that list is:

> "ii. femoral head-neck offset with an alpha angle greater than 50 degrees"

My MRI arthrogram of the hip, dated June 13, 2026, reports an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an **alpha angle of 68 degrees**. That is the exact imaging study type and the exact finding the policy calls for, and 68 degrees is above the 50-degree threshold the policy states. The policy lists other qualifying findings as well — including "iv. acetabular retroversion (overcoverage with crossover sign)" and "v. coxa profunda or protrusion vi. damage of the acetabular rim" — and the policy requires only one or more of them.

**5. No advanced osteoarthritis**

The policy states:

> "2. No evidence of advanced osteoarthritis, defined as Tonnis grade II or III, or joint space of less than 2 mm, except when there is mechanical instability."

My June 13, 2026 imaging reports that the joint space is preserved and that the arthritis grade is **Tonnis grade 0**. This is well below the Tonnis grade II or III that the policy identifies as disqualifying.

**6. The procedure matches the documented anatomy**

The policy states:

> "E. Requested procedures must be consistent with the anatomical abnormalities documented."

The abnormalities documented on my MRI arthrogram are cam-type femoroacetabular impingement with an alpha angle of 68 degrees and an anterosuperior labral tear. The arthroscopic procedure my surgeon has requested addresses that cam morphology directly. Dr. Marchetti has documented that this procedure is needed for my hip.

**7. Documentation the policy asks to see**

The policy's list of information needed for review states:

> "• History and Physical • Documented symptoms and conservative treatments attempted specific to policy criteria 1. B. • Physical exam findings"

Each of these was included in the prior authorization packet: the history and physical, the record of 14 weeks and 20 visits of supervised physical therapy along with NSAIDs and the April 21, 2026 injection, and the physical examination findings.

## A note on the criteria the plan applied

The denial notice tells me that the request does not meet the plan's medical necessity criteria, but it does not tell me which specific criterion in SUR160 the reviewer found unmet. I also want to be transparent that some of the policy's lists continue beyond the text I have been able to quote here, and I have not attempted to reconstruct language I do not have in front of me. If the plan is relying on a requirement I have not addressed, I ask that the plan identify that criterion by its letter or number in SUR160 in its response, so that I have a fair chance to supply what is missing.

I would also note, for the record, that my chart documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Regence BlueShield overturn the denial and authorize the hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) requested by Dr. Marchetti. If the plan maintains the denial in whole or in part, I ask for a written explanation that identifies the specific SUR160 criterion the plan found unmet, states the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination, and explains my next level of appeal, including any right to external review.

I understand that my appeal must be received by **February 19, 2027**, which is within 180 days of the August 23, 2026 notice. I am submitting this letter using the Washington member appeal form from regence.com/member/members/member-appeals, to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I can also be reached at the phone number above if anything further is needed; I would rather be asked for a document than have this closed for a missing one.

Thank you for taking a second look at my file.

Sincerely,

**Jordan Brooks**
Member ID: W436997835
Reference number: POC-41FE448BEA-64337
Date of birth: [My date of birth]
Signature: ______________________
Date: ______________

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of the denial notice dated August 23, 2026
- Office notes and history and physical from Dr. Marchetti, orthopedic surgery
- Physical therapy discharge note (April 9, 2026 – July 16, 2026; 20 visits)
- MRI arthrogram report dated June 13, 2026
- Medication and injection records, including the corticosteroid injection of April 21, 2026
- [Any additional records my surgeon's office sends]
- [Signed authorization form, if I am asking someone to appeal on my behalf]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
